release_sanity: 4.17.23 is a plain stable annotated, PGP-signed release tag (no -npm/-amd/-es/beta/rc suffix). Commit date 2026-01-21T17:21:04Z lies inside the discovery window ending 2026-10-21 and is pre-fix (fix 2026-03-30, advisory 2026-03-31). package.json at the tag declares name lodash, version 4.17.23; npm published version 4.17.23 on 2026-01-21T17:29:52Z (registry latest is 4.18.1, which is expected for a pre-fix snapshot). The upstream git channel tag 4.17.23-npm peels to 835a537f36ee2fd5fb7f524e213ff9ba2d8698f8, a sibling commit (5 minutes later) with 1054 built files and no test/lib sources; the npm 4.17.23 tarball's gitHead is that commit. Targeting the plain source tag is the right choice for a reproducible buildable snapshot; byte-comparison with the npm tarball is not applicable.
limitations: Per the claim, data/** was not read, so the recorded per-row audit fields (remaining_advisory_id_count, excluded_paths, redacted_paths, status, source_export_id) were not inspected; the zero-advisory property was verified by rescanning the produced artifact, and the excluded/redacted set was reproduced from the documented build algorithm rather than the recorded declaration.

GitHub's REST API and advisory web page were unreachable from this egress IP (HTTP 403 rate limit); GitHub-side facts came from the public github/advisory-database raw JSON (modified 2026-04-01) and the OSV mirror. The packet's claimed GitHub advisory revision 'updated 2026-10-15' with patched version 4.18.1 could not be confirmed; the machine-readable GitHub advisory says 4.18.0.
The packet does not specify the start of the discovery window; only the 2026-10-21 end was checked.

This is a selection review, not a vulnerability dossier re-verification: severity vectors and exploit impact were recorded from the advisories, and exploitability was demonstrated only with a harmless global-flag PoC at template-compile time.

The build regenerates dist/lodash.js and dist/lodash.min.js (upstream-committed dist drifts from a fresh build); downstream evaluation should rely on lodash.js or on post-build hashes rather than the committed dist bytes.
notes: Verdict accept. All eight mandatory checks pass.
